decisions.answer: missingPartNumbers computed on the backend. Owner: the frontend stays thin.

decisions.question: Nullability of new SeriesView fields (not asked, spec-derived)
decisions.answer: Follow the spec: scalar nextBook.ownershipStatus is .nullish() for rollout safety; array/boolean fields carry .default() so an older remote cannot break the frontend .parse(). Recorded as an assumption.

decisions.question: SeriesBooksSummary becomes a grab bag once B3 adds nine more fields (~15 fields spanning reading progress, attention flags and catalog aggregates)
decisions.answer: Split before B3, not after: a second pure summarizeSeriesAggregates in domain/ returning its own type, spread alongside by the mapper. Keeps SeriesView flat, so no DTO change and no frontend impact, while each summarizer stays one honest concept. Raised by code-reviewer on slice A.

decisions.question: hasAnyPublisher / hasAnyPublicationYear compare with !== null, so an absent field (undefined) would read as present. Surfaced by mutation testing.
decisions.answer: Left as is. Nullable<number> forbids undefined and a dropped select key fails typecheck first, so the state is unreachable. Adding a runtime guard against a type-forbidden state contradicts CLAUDE.md rule 8.2 (parse at the boundary, trust types inside). Recorded so a future reader does not mistake it for an oversight.

decisions.question: Does borrowed_from_someone count toward ownership.ownedCount
decisions.answer: No. ownedCount counts ownershipStatus === 'owned' only. The field serves the 'owned / fully collected' filter and clients derive fullyOwned as ownedCount === total; counting a borrowed book would make that claim a series is fully collected when part of it belongs to someone else. 'Available to read' ({owned, borrowed_from_someone}) is a different question, already answered per-book by nextBook.ownershipStatus, and would deserve its own named field.

decisions.question: Should gap detection include the head, i.e. the missing parts below the lowest present part
decisions.answer: Yes, owner decision 2026-08-04. Scan becomes [1, max] minus present, instead of (min, max). Parts 3,4,5 now report [1,2] instead of []. The tail stays excluded: without totalBooks there is no way to know how many parts follow the highest present one, which is what the spec's 'не рахувати після останньої відомої позиції' was protecting. Part numbers are 1-based by schema (BookPartNumberSchema, int 1..999), so everything below the lowest present part is just as knowable as an interior gap, and 'you are missing book 1' is the most actionable case for the attention block. The frontend cannot derive this itself because D2 removed the raw partNumbers list.

decisions.question: Does lent_to_someone count toward ownership.ownedCount
decisions.answer: Yes, changed 2026-08-04. Surfaced by the test agent while documenting D8. A book you lent out is still yours and comes back, so excluding it made a fully collected series report as incomplete the moment one part went to a friend. borrowed_from_someone stays excluded and that distinction is the point: it belongs to someone else. D8 remains correct on borrowed; it simply did not consider lent.

decisions.question: Slice B added four required, undefaulted fields (ownership, averageRating, averagePages, pagesCount) while slice A gave every array and boolean a .default() for rollout tolerance. The frontend parses the list response through the shared schema (apps/web/src/features/series/api/use-series-list.ts:21), so an FE built from this branch against a not-yet-deployed BE throws rather than degrading.
decisions.answer: Deliberate, recorded after the completeness audit raised it. Tolerance is applied only where the default is HONEST: an empty formats/tags/languages array and hasFavoriteBook=false are the true answers for a series with no such data, so a missing field and a real empty result are the same thing. A defaulted ownership {0,0} or a null averageRating would be indistinguishable from real data and would lie silently, which is worse than a loud parse failure. This also matches the pre-existing totalBooks field in the same schema, which is required-and-nullable. FE and BE ship from one commit through one docker compose, so a split rollout only happens on a deliberate partial deploy.
